purpose: Teach: 司祭/殿下/教皇/暗黒/破滅/連行/暴落/批准

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、中世の司祭の役割を論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: Ren, you were writing your paper on the role of medieval priests, weren't you?
lines.style: Warm, genuinely curious. Soft opening. Leans forward slightly with interest. A teacher checking in on a student she actually sees.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、王室の殿下の生活を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I actually ended up focusing on the daily life of royal princes instead.
lines.style: Quiet precision. A slight apologetic edge — explaining a redirect. Clear-eyed, meeting her gaze. Not defensive, just factual.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、ローマ教皇の歴史を論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: I see. So you shifted toward papal history then?
lines.style: Gentle probe, not correction. Thoughtful pace. She's tracking his thinking, not testing him. A beat of encouragement in the silence.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、暗黒時代の社会を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Actually, I found myself drawn to social structures during the Dark Ages instead.
lines.style: Careful, methodical. A hint of self-awareness — he's tracking his own shifts too. Slight vocal shrug. Not evasive, just honest about the meandering.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 帝国の破滅を論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: And from there you explored imperial collapse?
lines.style: Following the thread. Engaged but not surprised. A gentle confirmation that she's listening to where his thinking actually went.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、反逆者の連行を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Well, that eventually led me to focus on the arrest and deportation of dissidents during that period.
lines.style: More confident now. He's found solid ground. Precise diction. The kind of specific focus that shows real research behind it. Steady.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、市場の暴落を論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: Your work kept evolving, I noticed — market economics at some point?
lines.style: Observant but not accusatory. She's reflecting back the pattern she's noticed. Warm, appreciative of his circling approach. A teacher who understands how research actually works.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、条約の批准過程を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, though what I really settled on was the treaty ratification process and how it shaped everything.
lines.style: Final landing. Calm, certain. The sound of someone who's found what the paper actually needed to be. Slight relief underneath — he's arrived somewhere real.
